newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 10.
newsitem.headline: Reuters German Advertising & Media Digest -June 10.

text.p: REUTERS GERMAN ADVERTISING & MEDIA DIGEST
News from Reuters and the German press on Advertising, Marketing, Media, the Internet, Brand-name Products and Consumer Trends
ADVERTISING & MARKETING

FRANKFURT - Industry sources say Lufthansa is looking for a new stable of ad agencies. Along with current account holders Ogilvy & Mather and Young & Rubicam, Springer & Jacoby is reportedly also being considered, particularly for the company's Business Class campaign. (Horizont)
FRANKFURT - Duesseldorf-based agency Rempen & Partner is opening
at least one and possibly two offices in Munich. The first customer is reported to be Microsoft. (Horizont)
MEDIA & THE INTERNET:

BONN - Deutsche Telekom denies a report in news magazine "Spiegel" that it will begin asking 90 million marks ($52.7 million) for access to its cable network from pay-television stations. A Telekom spokesman says the figure represents the company's costs for a network connection, but that home end users cover some of these costs with the fees they are required to pay. (Reuter)

BONN - A German Internet bill due to voted on in parliament vote in the next two weeks could undermine controversial pornography charges against a local CompuServe Corp executive, the man's lawyer says. Under the Information and Communications Services Law, which already has the governing coalition's approval, Internet access providers generally would not be held liable for child pornography or other banned material on the Internet.
(Reuter)

COLOGNE - New media are presenting legal questions that are far from being resolved, say participants in a conference by the Institute of Broadcasting Rights at Cologne University. Digital television and Internet services present particular challenges. (Frankfurter Allgemeine Zeitung)

MUNICH - Deutsche Telekom and Picture Tel are expanding their cooperation on video communication, PictureTel GmbH says. A new contract covers sales, licensing, service, advertising and marketing of all video conference systems and future developments by PictureTel. (Reuter)
BRAND-NAME PRODUCTS & MARKETS:

WIESBADEN - German retail price inflation ticked up in May to post an annual rate of 1.6 percent after prices increased by 0.4 percent from the previous month, the Federal Statistics Office says. The rise in year-on-year inflation followed a three-month streak of falls, but was still below a January high of 1.8 percent. Prices had risen in April by 1.4 percent on a year earlier, but were unchanged month-on-month. (Reuter)
DRESDEN - The start of Dresdner Bank's Direktbank is delayed until at least the beginning of 1998. (Reuter)

STUTTGART - Plant manufacturing group Duerr AG says it has won a contract worth more than 260 million marks from Volkswagen AG unit Audi to build a spraying unit in Brasil. In a mandatory statement, the company says the contract had been awarded to its Duerr Systems GmbH unit. The Curitiba-based plant is scheduled for completion at the end of 1998 and would have capacity to spray up to 160,000 Audi A3, Volkswagen Vento and Golf models a year. (Reuter)

HAMBURG - Insurance group Volksfuersorge AG, a unit of AMB Holding, says it expects moderate growth and a good profit in 1997. Chief executive Hans Jaeger tells the company's shareholder meeting new life insurance business have risen in the first five months of the year and claims have dropped both in life and non-life segments. (Reuter)
PEOPLE NEWS:
WALLDORF - Manuela Koller is the new director of the marketing department of women's programming at channel tm3. (Kress)
